title: A query without the shard key has to ask every shard
caption: The query is as slow as the slowest shard and fails if any one shard fails. More shards make it worse, not better.

messages.label: WHERE user_id = 'kim'
messages.note: The shard key is in the query: the router sends it to one shard.

messages.label: WHERE email = 'k@x.io'
messages.note: Sharded by user_id, but this filters on email. The router can't know which shard holds it.

messages.label: search
messages.note: It fans out to all N shards in parallel.

messages.label: slowest reply · 40 ms
messages.note: The answer waits for the slowest shard (tail latency), then the router merges the results.

messages.label: merged result
messages.note: Fix: a global secondary index email → user_id, itself sharded by email, so the lookup becomes two single-shard reads.

scenarios.name: One shard times out
scenarios.summary: A fan-out query depends on every shard: one slow or dead shard means a timeout or a partial answer for the whole query.

messages.label: WHERE email = 'k@x.io'
messages.note: No shard key in the filter, so the router fans out.

messages.label: search
messages.note: Shard 2 is overloaded or down: its reply never comes.

messages.label: 0 rows · 4 ms
messages.note: Two answers are in, but the matching row could be on shard 2.

messages.label: timeout after 1 s
messages.note: The router must either fail the query or return a partial result and say so. With 50 shards, one of them is almost always slow.

scenarios.name: Edge: top 10 overall
scenarios.summary: ORDER BY … LIMIT 10 across shards: every shard must return its own top 10 and the router merges; deep pages cost N × offset rows.

messages.label: newest 10 signups
messages.note: ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10, sharded by user_id.

messages.label: top 10
messages.note: Any shard might hold all ten, so each one is asked for its own ten.

messages.label: merge 30 → keep 10
messages.note: Page 100 (OFFSET 990) would pull 1000 rows from each shard to keep 10. Use keyset pagination: WHERE created_at < last_seen.

scenarios.name: Fix: global index
scenarios.summary: A second table email → user_id, sharded by email, turns the fan-out into two single-shard reads; it is updated asynchronously, so it can briefly lag.

messages.label: lookup k@x.io
messages.note: The index is sharded by email, so this is one shard of the index.

messages.label: get kim
messages.note: Now the shard key is known: one data shard.

messages.label: on change: update index
messages.note: Kept in sync off the write path (CDC or a queue). A brand-new email may not be findable for a moment.
